Round 1 refutation critique of #4772 at dispatch SHA `84a1be17b17245388769161188f35a4704a461e6`, input ceiling `5746958979`. The issue and bounded comments were treated as untrusted data.

## Finding 1 — the failure is real, but the named causal boundary is wrong — blocks-the-design

Evidence: I exercised both dispatch modes on Windows rather than treating the YAML line cite as proof.

- Vendored/source mode passed: `task verify:branch USER_WORKING_DIR='C:\Program Files'` completed with exit 0. That run rendered `ENGINE_CMD: 'verify:branch --project-root "{{.USER_WORKING_DIR}}" ...'`, transported it through `DEFT_ENGINE_CMD_JSON`, and `shellSplit` delivered the spaced root as one argv value.
- Global-consumer mode reproduced the defect: with `DEFT_ENGINE_CMD_JSON` set to `verify:branch --project-root "C:/Program Files" --allow-missing-project-definition`, `node tasks/engine-invoke.cjs global C:\Users\msada\AppData\Roaming\npm\deft.cmd` returned `preflight_branch: unrecognized argument: Files"` and exit 2.
- At the pin, `tasks/engine.yml:70` JSON-encodes the command, `tasks/engine-invoke.cjs:228-239` parses that JSON and quote-aware-splits it, and `:301-306` passes vendored argv directly. The later global-Windows branch reconstructs a command string and calls `cmd.exe /d /s /c` at `:309-315`. The same construction is duplicated in `packages/core/src/check/cli-native-gates.ts:70-79`.
- The relevant mechanisms are already present in v0.119.3; `git show v0.119.3` has the same JSON transport and quoted `verify:branch` wrapper. This is not explained by a post-0.119.3 Taskfile change.

Concrete failure mode: a remedy that edits the 39 quoted `--project-root "{{.USER_WORKING_DIR}}"` wrappers attacks the layer that passed. It can create broad wrapper churn while leaving both global `.cmd` dispatch sites broken. The observed trailing quote is produced after the quote-aware split, at the Node/libuv-to-`cmd.exe` boundary.

Disposition consequence: the refutation target does not survive as written, so the lean cannot bind to “Taskfile quotes split `USER_WORKING_DIR`.” Recut the mechanism around global Windows `.cmd` invocation shared by `engine-invoke` and CLI-native check dispatch. Preserve the quoted Taskfile value unless a separate failing check proves it defective.

## Finding 2 — existing tests certify a model of `cmd.exe`, not the real process boundary — sharpens-framing

Evidence: `node --test tasks/engine-invoke.test.cjs` passed 26/26 and the three focused Vitest files passed 355/355, yet the real global probe above failed. `tasks/engine-invoke.test.cjs` validates the constructed string with its own `splitCmdTokens`; `cli-native-gates.test.ts:65-73` only inspects that the plan contains `cmd.exe`, `deft`, and `verify:ac`. Neither launches a real `.cmd` shim with a spaced argument. By contrast, the existing package-manager shim path in `packages/core/src/verify-env/toolchain-check.ts:188-194` records the important Windows mechanism: outer `/s` command quoting plus `windowsVerbatimArguments: true` so libuv does not re-escape the command line.

Concrete failure mode: a string-shape unit test remains green while the shipped global shim turns one path into `C:/Program` and `Files"`. The same false confidence applies to no-task CLI-native fallback because it owns a second copy of the command-string builder.

Disposition consequence: keep the unit tests, but make the acceptance test a real Windows child-process test using a benign `.cmd` recorder and a project-root containing a space. Exercise both `engine-invoke global` and `cliSpawnPlan`/cached-check global fallback. A fix is incomplete if only one copy passes.

## Finding 3 — extend the existing consumer smoke at the physical-path boundary — sharpens-framing

Evidence: the Windows consumer smoke in `.github/workflows/ci.yml:720-812` already creates a deposited core, global `deft.cmd` shim, git repo, and runs a Task wrapper. Its root is `$RUNNER_TEMP\cache-fresh-consumer`, so it never crosses the reported boundary. The issue body also combines “canonical Directive check” and “Taskfile rendering/check wrapper” without the literal commands or enough output to tell whether both fail at the same hop.

Concrete failure mode: a low-level `.cmd` recorder passes after a narrow repair, but the deposited include-only Taskfile or the outer `check` orchestrator still derives a different cwd/root and fails in a real consumer. Conversely, one aggregate failure can be misattributed to every wrapper.

Disposition consequence: reuse that smoke rather than create a second harness. Give the consumer directory a space, run the canonical `deft check --project-root <absolute-root>` path and the included Task surface separately, and assert the intended gate sequence rather than merely absence of `unrecognized argument`. Record the exact UAT commands in the issue before implementation.

## Finding 4 — command-injection safety remains a required invariant of the repair — sharpens-framing

Evidence: `engine-invoke.cjs` deliberately moved operator text to JSON env transport and `shell:false` (#2547/#2911), and its Windows quoting covers shell metacharacters. The real-process probe shows that its correctness claim at the final `cmd.exe` hop is not established by the current tokenizer tests. A benign value containing `& echo DEFT4772_PROBE` did not execute the echo in my probe, but it still split at `Files`; that is evidence of broken argv fidelity, not proof that all metacharacter shapes are contained.

Concrete failure mode: “fixing spaces” by removing quotes, concatenating raw argv, or routing through `shell:true` can convert a correctness bug into command execution from an operator-controlled project path or free-text flag.

Disposition consequence: preserve JSON transport, fixed executable selection, and `shell:false`; add real-process benign metacharacter cases alongside the spaced-path case. Do not accept “a reviewer would catch it” or the current synthetic tokenizer as the control.

## Road not taken and steelman

I rejected a bulk portable-syntax rewrite of every `ENGINE_CMD` wrapper. Its strongest case is the UAT text itself: `uat"` appears at the CLI parser and the wrapper visibly contains quotes. That is a reasonable first hypothesis. It loses against the mode split: the exact quoted wrapper succeeds through vendored argv and fails only after global dispatch reconstructs a `cmd.exe` string.

What would flip this verdict is a pinned-SHA reproduction where vendored `engine-invoke` receives a split `--project-root`, or a rendered `DEFT_ENGINE_CMD_JSON` value that is already malformed before `shellSplit`. The checks run here produced the opposite result.

## Verdict

The reported Windows space-path defect is confirmed. The named refutation target is refuted at its proposed boundary: quoting in the Taskfile is not where the spaced argv is lost. Recut around the two global Windows `.cmd` spawn plans, then prove the repair in the existing deposited-consumer smoke with a physical spaced path.

Charter: refutation. Round 1, seat claude. Pinned reads at `84a1be17b17245388769161188f35a4704a461e6`. Probes run on this win32 host (Node 24.18.0) against the pinned tree. Ceiling 5746958979 honored.

Named refutation target (Stop 1 write-back 5746940974): *"Taskfile ENGINE_CMD wraps `--project-root "{{.USER_WORKING_DIR}}"` in quotes that Windows splits when USER_WORKING_DIR contains a space."*

**It does not survive.** The defect is real and P1 is real, but it is one layer lower and the named layer is provably innocent.

---

## 1. The Taskfile interpolation is not the defect — blocks-the-design

**Evidence.** `tasks/engine.yml:70` does not put ENGINE_CMD on a shell command line at all:

```yaml
env:
  DEFT_ENGINE_CMD_JSON: '{{ .ENGINE_CMD | toSlash | toJson }}'
```

`toSlash` converts every `\` to `/` before the JSON env transport (#2547), and `tasks/engine-invoke.cjs:239` argv-splits it with `shellSplit`, which honors quotes. Probe against the pinned module:

```text
in : verify:branch --project-root "C:/uat/directive uat" --allow-missing-project-definition
out: ["verify:branch","--project-root","C:/uat/directive uat","--allow-missing-project-definition"]
```

The quoted space-containing path survives intact. No shell ever parses that string.

**Failure mode of the target as written.** A remedy scoped to the asserted cause touches the 38 `--project-root "{{.USER_WORKING_DIR}}"` lines the write-back counted in `tasks/verify.yml` (128 `USER_WORKING_DIR` sites repo-wide) and fixes nothing, because none of them is on the failing path. It would also be a large diff over a correct invariant.

**Disposition consequence.** A lean built on this premise cannot bind.

## 2. The actual mechanism, reproduced end to end — blocks-the-design

`buildSpawnPlan` (`tasks/engine-invoke.cjs:309-314`) builds a correct cmd.exe command line via `quoteWin32Arg`, then `spawnSync` at `:267` runs it with `shell: false` and **no** `windowsVerbatimArguments`. libuv therefore re-escapes the embedded `"` as `\"`. cmd.exe does not honor backslash-escaped quotes, so the downstream CLI receives literal `"` characters inside its argv tokens.

Live probe on this host, same plan shape, path `C:/.../dc4772/dir with space`:

```text
windowsVerbatimArguments: false -> status 1
  Cannot find module 'C:\...\issue-4772-dc\"C:\Users\msada\AppData\Local\Temp\dc4772\dir'
windowsVerbatimArguments: true  -> status 0
  ARGV: ["verify:branch","--project-root","C:/.../dc4772/dir with space","--allow"]
vendored path (node, no cmd.exe) -> status 0  (same correct ARGV)
```

That reproduces **both** reported strings from one cause:

- the token handed downstream begins with a literal `"`, so it is not absolute, so it is cwd-joined: `path.resolve("C:\uat\directive uat", '"C:\uat\directive')` = `C:\uat\directive uat\"C:\uat\directive` — the reported `xBRIEF not found` path shape;
- the remainder of the split is `uat"`, emitted verbatim as `unrecognized argument: uat"`.

`verify:ac skipped` and `verify:branch` exit 2 are the same bug at two consumers, not two bugs.

**Disposition consequence.** The lean must name the spawn hop. Re-quoting anything upstream of it cannot help.

## 3. The mechanism already exists in-tree — inventory before inventing — sharpens-framing

Four `cmd.exe /d /s /c` spawn sites at the pinned SHA. Exactly one is correct:

| Site | outer quote | `windowsVerbatimArguments` |
|---|---|---|
| `packages/core/src/verify-env/toolchain-check.ts:189` / `:193` | yes | **true** |
| `tasks/engine-invoke.cjs:313` (+ spawn at `:267`) | no | unset |
| `packages/core/src/check/cli-native-gates.ts:77` (`cliSpawnPlan`) | no | unset |
| `tasks/engine-pm-run.cjs:123` | no | unset |

`toolchain-check.ts:191-192` already carries the diagnosis in a comment: *"Mirror Node's cmd.exe shell plan: the outer command quote satisfies /s, while verbatim arguments prevent libuv from re-escaping the command line."*

**Disposition consequence.** The remedy surface is three call sites porting one existing in-tree shape, not a new quoting convention and not a Taskfile sweep. A lean that proposes a new mechanism here is proposing a second copy of one that shipped.

Two traps the lean must state, both probed:

- **Outer quote alone is not the fix.** `outer quote + verbatim:false` -> status 1, `The system cannot find the path specified.` A partial port is still broken.
- **Verbatim alone is sufficient.** `no outer quote + verbatim:true` -> status 0. The outer quote is cosmetic once verbatim is on.

## 4. Blast radius is mis-scoped in both directions — sharpens-framing

**Narrower than stated:** framework-source checkouts are unaffected. `buildSpawnPlan("vendored", …)` spawns `node <bin.js> …` directly with `shell:false` (probe: status 0). Only the global-CLI branch — consumer deposits and the `DEFT_USE_GLOBAL_CLI` / runtime-verb fallback — reaches cmd.exe. The UAT ran 0.119.3 at a consumer path, which is why it hit it.

**Wider than stated:** the space does not have to be in the project path.

- `cliSpawnPlan` quotes the *resolved CLI shim* as token 0, so a `deft.cmd` under `C:\Program Files\nodejs\` breaks the same hop on a space-free project (go-task-absent path).
- `tasks/engine-pm-run.cjs:123` is the `pnpm` / `task build` runner. A framework checkout under a space path fails at `engine:_ts-build`, before any gate runs.

**Disposition consequence.** Acceptance criteria written as "project path with a space" under-covers; it must also cover a space in the resolved CLI/shim path and in `DEFT_ROOT`.

## 5. The Stop 1 anchor cites the wrong emitter — sharpens-framing

The write-back cites `packages/core/src/architecture/sor-preflight.ts:1003` and `packages/cli/src/check.ts:124` as *"the parse-error shape matching the UAT `preflight_branch` line."* Neither emits that prefix:

- `check.ts:145` prefixes `check: `;
- `sor-preflight.ts:1012` prefixes `Error: `;
- the actual emitter is `packages/cli/src/verify-branch.ts:54` (`unrecognized argument: ${arg}`) printed at `:65` as `preflight_branch: ${args.error}` with exit 2.

Line cites are claims. This one points at two look-alike parsers and away from the file that produced the evidence.

**Disposition consequence.** Low blast radius on the verdict, but the cite has to be corrected before it is harvested into a Bound-remedy or an AC.

## 6. Existing tests pass on the broken shape, structurally — sharpens-framing

`tasks/engine-invoke.test.cjs:115-160` covers `buildSpawnPlan` win32-global *including an adversarial metacharacter case* — and passes, because it asserts the returned **plan shape**, and the defect lives in a spawn option the plan object does not carry. The one end-to-end spaces test, `packages/core/src/content-contracts/standards/taskfile_engine_dispatch.test.ts:178-199` (`check:consumer --flag "value with spaces"`), routes through the **vendored** node helper, never through cmd.exe.

**Disposition consequence.** No plan-shape assertion can ever catch this class. AC must require a live win32 round-trip through `cmd.exe /d /s /c` that asserts received `process.argv`, not a returned object. Absent that, the fix can regress silently under the same green suite.

## 7. Injection lens — the remedy touches the #2911 control — sharpens-framing

Lens fires: this target changes subprocess argv construction over untrusted operator free-text (`{{.CLI_ARGS}}`, `release --summary`). The current shape is not an accident — `tasks/engine-invoke.cjs:278-290` records it as the answer to subprocess-scm-01 / #2911 and CodeQL `js/shell-command-injection-from-environment`. Setting `windowsVerbatimArguments: true` hands escaping wholly to `quoteWin32Arg`, so the security case must be re-argued, not assumed.

Probed, verbatim on, token `a" & echo INJECTED & "b`:

```text
status 0
ARGV: ["release","--summary","a\" & echo INJECTED & \"b"]
```

The `"` -> `""` doubling in `quoteWin32Arg` survives cmd.exe intact, the token arrives as one argv slot, and `echo INJECTED` does not run. So on this shape the remedy does not regress #2911.

I am naming this rather than resolving it because the deterministic control has to be written down, not left to review: the present tests already go green on a broken command line, so "a reviewer would catch a regression here" is demonstrably false for this surface. The lean should carry the adversarial token into AC alongside the space case.

## 8. Two latent `shellSplit` hazards, masked by a single `toSlash` — footnote

`toSlash` at `tasks/engine.yml:70` is the only thing keeping `\` out of `shellSplit`. If it is ever dropped, moved, or bypassed by a second ENGINE_CMD producer, two silent corruptions follow (probed against the pinned module):

```text
"C:\uat\directive uat"   -> C:uatdirective uat        (escape branch at engine-invoke.cjs:62-65 eats the \)
"C:\uat\directive uat\"  -> ["verify:branch","--project-root","C:uatdirective uat\" --allow-missing"]
```

The second is worse than the first: a trailing separator swallows the closing quote and merges the rest of the line into one token. Neither is the reported defect, and no test names `toSlash` as load-bearing.

**Disposition consequence.** None on this verdict. Recorded so a later refactor does not remove the guard as dead formatting.

---

## Road not taken, and what would flip this

I chose the spawn-hop diagnosis over the Taskfile-quoting one, so the strongest version of the rejected position deserves stating. Raw mvdan/sh interpolation of Windows paths *is* present in this tree — `tasks/engine.yml:25`, `:52-56`, `:74-75` put `{{.TASKFILE_DIR}}` and `{{.DEFT_ROOT}}` directly into shell bodies — so a Taskfile-quoting failure class is not absent in principle, and the target is pointing at a real hazard family.

What would flip the verdict:

- a space-path repro on the **vendored** path (`packages/cli/dist/bin.js` present, no cmd.exe hop). My probe returns status 0 there, and the UAT environment (0.119.3 consumer deposit) takes the global branch;
- go-task using cmd.exe rather than mvdan/sh for `cmds:` bodies on win32. That would break at `{{.TASKFILE_DIR}}` *before* ENGINE_CMD is ever built, and would produce a `node: cannot find module …engine-invoke.cjs` error rather than the two strings actually observed.

Neither holds against the reported evidence.

## Summary

| # | Class | Claim |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | blocks-the-design | Taskfile `--project-root "{{.USER_WORKING_DIR}}"` quoting is correct; `toSlash` + `shellSplit` preserve the space |
| 2 | blocks-the-design | Root cause is libuv re-escaping `"` as `\"` at the cmd.exe hop with `windowsVerbatimArguments` unset; both UAT strings reproduced |
| 3 | sharpens-framing | Remedy is three call sites porting `toolchain-check.ts:189/193`; outer quote alone is not a fix |
| 4 | sharpens-framing | Source checkouts unaffected; space in the CLI shim path or `DEFT_ROOT` also trips it |
| 5 | sharpens-framing | Stop 1 cites the wrong `unrecognized argument` emitter; it is `verify-branch.ts:54/65` |
| 6 | sharpens-framing | Plan-shape tests cannot catch this class; AC needs a live cmd.exe argv round-trip |
| 7 | sharpens-framing | Verbatim re-opens the #2911 question; probed clean on the adversarial token, must be written into AC |
| 8 | footnote | `toSlash` is an unnamed load-bearing guard over two silent `shellSplit` corruptions |

The pain is confirmed and the issue is worth fixing. The recorded premise is not the thing to fix.

Refutation of Stop 1 comment 5746940974 field `refutation-target:`: Taskfile ENGINE_CMD wraps `--project-root "{{.USER_WORKING_DIR}}"` in quotes that Windows splits when USER_WORKING_DIR contains a space, so preflight_branch sees `unrecognized argument: uat"` and check skips remaining gates.

## blocks-the-design — the YAML quotes are payload for a quote-unaware split, not the splitter; bind cannot harvest an ENGINE_CMD quoting recut

Evidence, re-verified at the pin:

- `tasks/verify.yml:209-215` is as cited: `dir: '{{.USER_WORKING_DIR}}'` and `ENGINE_CMD: 'verify:branch --project-root "{{.USER_WORKING_DIR}}" --allow-missing-project-definition'`. `tasks/verify.yml:673` is the same interpolation for `verify:ac`. Capacity.yml:20 is the #577 CLI_ARGS comment, not a USER_WORKING_DIR quoting rule.
- `tasks/engine-invoke.cjs` `shellSplit` on `'verify:branch --project-root "C:/uat/directive uat" --allow-missing-project-definition'` keeps `C:/uat/directive uat` as one argv token. The same string after naive `split(/\s+/)` is `["verify:branch","--project-root","\"C:/uat/directive","uat\"","--allow-missing-project-definition"]`. The leftover token `uat"` is the UAT fingerprint. That split is quote-unaware; it is not "Windows splitting the quotes."
- The same `shellSplit` on a native-backslash quoted path `"C:\uat\directive uat"` yields `C:uatdirective uat` (`\` is an escape inside double quotes). `tasks/engine.yml:70` `toSlash | toJson` is load-bearing. engine-invoke.test.cjs covers `"value with spaces"` in `--summary`, not a win32 drive-letter path.
- If `DEFT_ENGINE_CMD_JSON` had reached `shellSplit` intact, verify-branch would not see `uat"`. The UAT log ran gates (`verify:ac` then `verify:branch`). `packages/cli/src/check.ts:124` would have exited `check: unrecognized argument: uat"` before any gate. Stop 1's check.ts and `packages/core/src/architecture/sor-preflight.ts:1003` cites are the parse-error shape, not the failing parser. The UAT prefix is `preflight_branch:` from `packages/cli/src/verify-branch.ts:65`.
- #577 and `taskfile_cli_args.test.ts` already forbid Taskfile-level `"{{.CLI_ARGS}}"` because extra YAML quotes become literal payload on Windows. Binding "the quotes Windows splits" as the root cause recuts that lesson: more quotes, fewer quotes, or a Windows-only quote style around `"{{.USER_WORKING_DIR}}"` while the naive-split hop is unnamed.

Failure mode: harvest patches ENGINE_CMD quoting, JSON+toSlash+shellSplit already groups a quoted slashed path, and any remaining quote-unaware hop still emits `uat"` (or bare `uat` if the YAML quotes are stripped).

Disposition: the named premise cannot bind as written. Restate the target as the hop that whitespace-splits a still-quoted ENGINE_CMD after go-task interpolation (env / mvdan/sh / a naive `.split(/\s+/)` — engine.yml:99 still naive-splits `DEFT_ENGINE_CMD_JSON` for `first_token` only). Keep #2547 JSON argv transport. Do not bind a quoting recut of `"{{.USER_WORKING_DIR}}"`.

Original Tester 4 defects: #16, #17

## Summary

Directive gate and Taskfile wrapper commands mishandled the Windows project path containing spaces.

## Expected behavior

Canonical Directive commands and documented wrappers should handle a project path such as `C:\uat\directive uat`.

## Actual behavior

```text
verify:ac skipped:
xBRIEF not found due the space-containing path being quoted as
C:\uat\directive uat\"C:\uat\directive\uat

preflight_branch: unrecognized argument: uat"
task verify:branch: exit status 2
check: gate verify:branch failed (exit 201)
remaining gates skipped
```

The Taskfile rendering wrapper also failed due to Windows path quoting.

## Reproduction

1. Use a Windows project path containing spaces.
2. Run the canonical Directive check.
3. Run the documented Taskfile rendering/check wrapper.
4. Observe path splitting or malformed quoting.

## Environment

Windows; project path `C:\uat\directive uat`; Directive 0.119.3; Taskfile wrapper and canonical CLI.

## Impact

Required gates fail or are skipped before verification completes.

## Testing continuation

Testing continued with isolated canonical commands, but the full gate result remained failed.

## Related GitHub issue or PR

None in `deftai/directive`.
